newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-ALMSICK ALMOST QUIT BEFORE OLYMPICS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-ALMSICK ALMOST QUIT BEFORE OLYMPICS.

text.p: Franziska van Almsick, who became one of Germany's biggest sports names in her early teens, revealed on Friday that she went close to dropping out of swimming last year before the Atlanta Olympics.

Van Almsick, who struggled at the 1996 German trials before winning a silver medal in the 200 freestyle in Atlanta, said she had suffered with pyschological as well as physical problems in the build-up to the Games.

"1996 was a hard year. I had motivation problems. If it hadn't been the Olympics I would probably have stopped," the 18-year-old former East German said. "It was no fun. I was swimming for other people, not myself."
The Berlin swimmer has a huge profile at home where she has made millions out of advertising since she won two silver and two bronze medals at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics aged 14.
The negative side of her success has been the constant media attention which the swimmer has faced for most of her career.

Van Almsick took a long break after Atlanta and has only recently returned to training. She has decided to skip the current World Cup short-course season and is not competing at this weekend's meeting on her home soil in Gelsenkirchen.

But she was still the centre of attention at a press conference on the eve of the meeting. Even when officials were talking to the media from a table at the front of the room at the start of the conference, cameras were fixed on van Almsick at the back.
The German, who was 11 when the Berlin Wall fell in the autumn of 1989, said she had not missed the sport during her layoff in the second half of last year.
"(During the break) I just did things which I enjoy doing. I stayed in bed if I wanted to and when I fancied training, I went to the pool," she said.
"It was hard to start training again. I learned a lot in 1996. Now I want to start again."
Van Almsick said it was too early to say whether she would compete at the 2000 Sydney Olympics.
Her main goal was to regain top form for the European long-course championships in Spain in August and the world championships in Perth, Australia in January 1998.
The German will only compete at low-key meetings in Germany in the next few months and stay out of tough international competition for a while.
"I want to get back to my top level as soon as possible but I have to be very patient," van Almsick said.
